template_name: The McMansion Effect — Explicit Rejection of Implicit Pleasure
antecedent_conditions: Architectural design D has high surface appeal (large scale, symmetrical, materially rich, conforming to evolutionary preference signals) but violates compositional principles known to architecturally educated observers (incoherent proportional system, arbitrary ornament, facade composition without underlying spatial logic).
predicted_outcome:
- Architecturally naïve observers: positive implicit response + positive explicit evaluation. Channels aligned. High ratings, high confidence, fast response.
- Architecturally educated observers: positive implicit response (perceptual fluency, material richness) + negative explicit evaluation ("it's tasteless," "the proportions are wrong"). Channel conflict. ACC activation, response latency increase, confidence decrease.
- Between-group difference in evaluation: large (d ≈ 0.8–1.2).
- Between-group difference in implicit measures: small (d ≈ 0.1–0.3) — both groups have positive implicit responses.
- The educated group's negative evaluation is driven by the explicit aesthetic framework overriding implicit pleasure.
neural_signature: Educated group shows dlPFC activation concurrent with positive medial OFC signal, with dACC mediating the conflict. Naïve group shows aligned OFC + vmPFC positive signal without dlPFC conflict engagement.
architectural_consequence: Design quality as judged by informed observers is not the same as design quality as experienced by naïve occupants. Both are "real" — they reflect different points on the expertise sedimentation continuum. Design education literally changes the brain's response to architecture. This is not elitism; it is a neuroscientific fact about how training reshapes implicit processing.
name: The McMansion Effect — Explicit Rejection of Implicit Pleasure
